The NETL CO2U open LCA database maintains detailed life cycle inventories for the electricity mixes mentioned above, which include emissions associated with production and transmission. Thus, scope 2 emissions are well accounted for in the model. The emissions associated with manufacturing of several novel components of the DAC process are unknown. Therefore, several assumptions were used to approximate the emissions contributions of these components to the overall environmental impact of the technology over a proposed plant lifetime of 30 years. For example, the HCSS is composed of the pleated, sorbent-coated filter within a filter module. It was modeled using the bulk of its constituent plastics makeup to account for emissions incurred during manufacturing its constituent materials. The analysis, summarized by Figure 3, showed that even in the case of a renewables mix, filter module materials account for less than 1% of emissions in the current LCA model. Further information on filter manufacturing activities and associated resource intensity and emissions can be obtained as this technology matures and will improve the ability of the technology team to scrutinize the impacts of various components of the process. Characterization factors for each flow leaving the system boundary were defined using the Tool for Reduction and Assessment of Chemicals and Other Environmental Impacts (TRACI, v2.1 (NETL)).
